checks_run.actual:
D-133's facts match the evidence:
- code-security's summary matches my round-7 record (PASS, no new finding; cadence 1-600 or start-up refused; the probe is not shipped; the split script exits 1 on any failure across the 8 combinations, i.e. 1 passing and 7 failing; and the dropped-argument observation).
- qa's F-DG4-148 numbers match qa's round-7 verification note and RUN-NOTES: 3/4 runs exit 1 in the contended series (boundary loads 7.70→24.19, 24.19→22.71 and 22.71→16.52); 1/4 in the held series (208 samples, median 14.38, p10 12.40, min 7.96 only at the controller's ramp-up); and 4/4 pass in the clean series (56 samples, 2.12-5.48).

D-134: the envelope (1-min load ≤ 8, sampled at least every 30 s for the whole run) sits below every load at which a pnpm test failure is in evidence:
- the held-series failure ran at 12.40-17.65;
- my round-7 failure was at 23-27;
- the round-6 failures were at ≥ 13.
Passes are in evidence at 2.12-5.48 (qa round 7, sampled) and at 3-9 (the round-6 reproduction in findings.json). So the bound is accurate and conservative.

The envelope weakens no test. The 5 s asyncUtilTimeout and the 30 s architecture-test timeout are unchanged (qa QA-R7-07; my SEC-R7-13). The required 30 s sampling is stricter than round 7's start/end-only samples.

The acceptance route is tool-enforced:
- rules.mjs:566 rejects any ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION that is not Low and non-mandatory;
- rules.mjs:582-585 require a release-auditor sidecar, a specialist sidecar, the findings.json accepted_by mirror and the gate's accepted_observations list.
F-DG4-148 is Low, mandatory_violation false and still OPEN in findings.json, so nothing has been accepted early. I write no verifications file this round, as the assignment says.

Observations, not defects, for the next records update:
(1) environment.md says the orchestrator's pre-freeze runs 'passed at load 1.4–2.3 in every round'. The 12 pre-freeze unit logs carry no load samples; 'load' matches only test names such as load.test.ts. The recorded pre-freeze loads are e2e start/end samples, 1.22-2.33 (r2 starts at 1.22). Every pre-freeze unit run did exit 0 (12/12), so the sentence is a proxy, not a measurement. It has no behavioural effect, because the envelope rests on qa's sampled runs.
(2) The re-run clause ('a run that fails above the envelope is disclosed, and the check is re-run inside it') must be read with the DG2 round-10 evidence-honesty condition. It legitimately covers the two named timing classes. Any failure of another kind still needs its own explanation. From the security angle, the residual risk (a load-only race masked by a re-run) is bounded: the concurrency, If-Match, exactly-once and handover-race tests live in the integration suite and my probes, which the envelope does not govern, and they passed at load 13-27 in round 7 (SEC-R7-09/10/17).

The 14 'fail' and 2 'timeout' hits in load-envelope-crosscheck.log are quoted round-7 text and file names, not failures of this check.
